do not suppress true dependence with a false-dependence pragma
skills.pattern: a hot loop is a reduction or accumulation where a serial accumulator prevents direct unrolling, but reassociation or partial accumulation is legal
required_steps: confirm the computation is a reduction
confirm reassociation is legal for the required numerical tolerance
create partial accumulators indexed by lane
unroll lane updates
partition partial accumulator storage
combine partial sums at the end
skills.strategy: replace the single serial accumulator with lane-local partial accumulators, unroll updates across lanes, and combine partial results using a final reduction or tree reduction

guards: do not use if work items have cross-item dependencies
ensure memory bandwidth can feed replicated PEs
avoid excessive local buffer replication
skills.pattern: the workload contains independent jobs, records, particles, points, alignments, or work items that can be processed by replicated processing elements
required_steps: identify independent work items
choose number of processing elements
reshape input/output buffers by PE or lane
partition PE dimension completely
unroll the PE loop
preserve per-item output mapping
skills.strategy: batch independent work items, allocate per-lane local buffers, unroll the processing-element loop, and partition buffers along the PE dimension

guards: unrolling cannot compensate for insufficient memory bandwidth
check whether the loop is compute-bound before increasing parallelism
avoid unroll factors that exceed memory supply
skills.pattern: the loop is limited by global-memory bandwidth or AXI burst behavior, and adding arithmetic lanes would increase memory pressure without feeding the lanes
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not apply unrolling as the primary optimization; first use coalescing, memory banking, local staging, or tiling to provide enough data bandwidth

guards: do not maximize unroll factor blindly
compare latency improvement against resource growth
consider smaller factors like 2, 4, or 8 before complete unroll
skills.pattern: a proposed unroll factor replicates too much arithmetic, local storage, or routing and creates excessive DSP/LUT/FF/BRAM usage or timing degradation
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: reduce the unroll factor, use partial unroll, share resources, or improve memory locality before further parallelization

guards: do not add ping-pong buffers unless overlap is possible
avoid excessive local memory use
preserve first and last tile behavior
avoid read/write hazards between buffers
skills.pattern: the kernel processes data in chunks or tiles, and load, compute, and store phases for consecutive chunks currently execute serially
required_steps: identify chunk/tile loop
split load, compute, and store stages
create at least two local buffers per overlapped data stream
alternate buffers using tile index parity
handle prologue and epilogue iterations
apply DATAFLOW if stages have legal producer/consumer dependencies
validate functional correctness and actual phase overlap
skills.strategy: split the design into load, compute, and store stages; allocate ping-pong buffers; overlap load of tile k+1, compute of tile k, and optionally store of tile k-1

guards: do not duplicate very large buffers if memory usage exceeds budget
do not overlap stages that access the same buffer instance
validate schedule and correctness
skills.pattern: a tiled or chunked computation has one local buffer, causing the next load to wait for current compute or store to finish
required_steps: identify the buffer that causes serialization
allocate two buffers of the same shape
use t & 1 or equivalent parity for buffer selection
ensure producer and consumer use different buffers in the same overlapped iteration
handle startup and drain iterations
skills.strategy: duplicate the local buffer into ping-pong buffers and alternate producer/consumer stages across them

guards: do not use DATAFLOW if stages are still sequentially dependent on the same buffer instance
do not create streams without bounded production/consumption behavior
avoid deadlock-prone stream cycles
skills.pattern: load, compute, and store logic is mixed in a single loop or function, preventing DATAFLOW scheduling or stage overlap
required_steps: extract load stage
extract compute stage
extract store stage
define buffer or stream interfaces between stages
ensure no hidden cross-stage dependence prevents overlap
apply DATAFLOW at parent scope
check dataflow report for actual concurrency
skills.strategy: split the code into explicit producer/consumer stages connected by local buffers or streams, then apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope when dependencies allow

guards: do not read from a buffer before it has been loaded
do not store a tile before it has been computed
do not drop the final tile during drain
skills.pattern: a double-buffered loop overlaps stages across tile indices and therefore requires prologue, steady-state, and epilogue handling
required_steps: extend loop bounds for startup/drain
guard load for t < NUM_TILES
guard compute for t > 0 and t <= NUM_TILES
guard store for t > 1 or equivalent
handle partial final tile
skills.strategy: guard load, compute, and store stages by tile index so the first and last overlapped iterations do not read uninitialized buffers or write invalid outputs

guards: ping-pong buffers alone do not guarantee overlap
check DATAFLOW report or schedule evidence
avoid adding memory overhead without reducing interval
skills.pattern: a proposed double-buffering transformation duplicates buffers but load, compute, and store phases still execute serially or cannot overlap because of dependencies
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not treat double buffering as complete unless stages actually overlap and interval/latency improves

guards: do not duplicate large 2D/3D tiles blindly
check local memory resource budget
prefer smaller tile size or stream buffering when possible
skills.pattern: double buffering would duplicate large local arrays and exceed or severely pressure BRAM/URAM resources
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: reduce tile size, buffer only the required stream, use smaller staging buffers, or avoid double buffering if memory duplication outweighs overlap benefit

guards: do not split arrays that must remain on the same physical memory for host compatibility
do not assume bundle names alone map to separate banks without platform/linker support
avoid bank imbalance where one bank remains the bottleneck
skills.pattern: multiple high-bandwidth arrays or streams are accessed independently but share one memory bundle or memory bank, creating bandwidth contention
required_steps: identify independent high-bandwidth arrays
estimate read/write traffic per array
place independent streams on separate m_axi bundles
map bundles to distinct physical banks if platform/host supports it
update host-side buffer bank assignment if required
verify bandwidth and correctness
skills.strategy: assign independent high-bandwidth m_axi ports to separate bundles or memory banks so concurrent memory streams can use independent bandwidth
skills.template:
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A offset=slave bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B offset=slave bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=C offset=slave bundle=gmem2
// Ensure host/linker maps gmem0/gmem1/gmem2 to distinct memory banks when required.

guards: do not move ports without updating host/linker bank assignment if needed
do not split dependent streams in a way that complicates correctness
ensure the chosen platform actually has multiple memory banks
skills.pattern: one memory bundle or bank carries most of the traffic while other banks are unused or underused
required_steps: estimate memory traffic by port
identify independent streams that can move banks
separate high-read and high-write streams when useful
update m_axi bundle names and host/linker mapping
validate performance and correctness
skills.strategy: redistribute independent arrays, read-only tables, or output streams across available memory banks so traffic is balanced and concurrent accesses avoid contention

guards: single bundle may serialize or contend independent accesses
separate only when host/platform support exists
keep low-traffic or dependent ports together when separation has no benefit
skills.pattern: multiple independent high-bandwidth m_axi ports are assigned to the same bundle or memory bank, causing avoidable contention
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: avoid placing all high-bandwidth arrays on one gmem bundle when the platform and host flow support multiple memory banks

guards: preserve host ABI unless changes are explicitly allowed
verify platform memory bank availability
update host allocation and linker connectivity when required
do not expose hidden test or benchmark provenance
skills.pattern: a proposed multi-bank transformation changes m_axi bundles or physical bank assignment without evidence that the host code, linker config, and target platform support the mapping
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not assume bundle changes alone are valid; require explicit platform/host/linker support for physical bank mapping

guards: do not complete-partition large arrays unnecessarily
do not partition dimensions not accessed in parallel
avoid partitioning when the bottleneck is off-chip memory bandwidth
skills.pattern: a local array needs more read/write ports for pipelined or unrolled access, but the correct partition style depends on access pattern and array size
required_steps: identify the parallel access pattern
identify the accessed array dimension
choose complete/cyclic/block partition based on size and indexing
match factor to unroll factor or port demand
check II and resource usage
skills.strategy: choose complete partition for small arrays or dimensions fully accessed in parallel, cyclic partition for regular interleaved lane accesses, and block partition for contiguous per-worker regions

guards: do not use this when the exact sequential update order is semantically required
floating-point reassociation can change bit-exact results
ensure the privatized arrays fit local memory or reduce the number of lanes/PEs
do not add dependence inter false to a real same-address update hazard
merge phase must cover all bins/elements and preserve boundary conditions
skills.pattern: a pipelined loop performs read-modify-write updates to an array element, such as hist[key] += v, acc[idx] = acc[idx] + v, or scatter accumulation, and the scheduler cannot prove that consecutive iterations update different addresses
required_steps: identify the array updated through read-modify-write in the II-limited loop
determine whether collisions can occur across iterations and whether accumulation is associative enough for partial merging
create lane-local, PE-local, bank-local, or tile-local copies of the accumulator
partition the privatized dimension completely so each lane has independent storage ports
rewrite the hot loop to update only its private accumulator copy
add a separate merge loop or tree reduction over private copies
pipeline the hot update loop and the merge loop where legal
validate numerical equivalence, especially for floating-point accumulation order
skills.strategy: privatize the accumulator array by lane, processing element, bank, or tile; perform independent read-modify-write updates locally; then merge the partial arrays in a separate reduction/merge phase so the hot update loop can pipeline without same-array inter-iteration hazards

guards: only scalarize when no other code observes the intermediate array updates during the loop
do not scalarize variable-index updates that may target many different elements; use privatization or banking instead
preserve initialization and final write-back behavior
for floating point, scalarization preserves serial order but may still be recurrence-limited by operator latency
skills.pattern: a loop repeatedly reads and writes the same scalar-like array element or a small fixed set of array elements, creating an avoidable memory read-after-write dependence through an array port
required_steps: identify array elements whose index is invariant or from a very small fixed set inside the loop
load the initial value into scalar or fully partitioned local state before the hot loop
rewrite the loop body to update the scalar/register state instead of reading and writing the array each iteration
write the final scalar/register state back after the loop or tile
pipeline the hot loop and inspect whether the memory dependence disappears
skills.strategy: scalarize the hot read-modify-write state into registers, update the scalar inside the pipelined loop, and write the array element back once after the loop or after the tile; for a small fixed set, completely partition the state and keep each element in a separate register

guards: do not apply when the operation is order-sensitive or non-associative under required correctness checks
floating-point results may differ from serial accumulation due to reassociation
ensure input bandwidth can feed the chosen lane factor
do not suppress the true accumulator dependence with a false-dependence pragma
skills.pattern: a hot pipelined loop has a scalar reduction or accumulation, and the loop-carried accumulator latency prevents the requested II or blocks useful unrolling/lane parallelism
required_steps: confirm the operation is a valid reduction such as sum, min, max, bitwise operation, or another associative/commutative form
choose a lane or unroll factor that matches available memory bandwidth and resources
create partial accumulators indexed by lane
completely partition the partial accumulator array
rewrite the main loop to update partial[lane] instead of one shared accumulator
pipeline the main loop and unroll the lane loop
perform final reduction across partial accumulators
check numerical tolerance for floating-point or non-associative expressions
skills.strategy: replace the single accumulator with lane-local partial accumulators, update them in parallel, and combine them with a final tree or cleanup reduction; preserve serial order only when exact order is required

guards: never apply inter false to a true read-after-write, write-after-read, or write-after-write dependence
do not use dependence pragmas as a generic II fix
for reductions or same-address updates, use partial accumulators or privatization instead
keep the pragma scoped to the exact variable and loop where non-overlap is proven
skills.pattern: the HLS scheduler reports a loop-carried memory dependence, but manual index analysis shows different iterations access non-overlapping elements or independent lanes
required_steps: identify the reported dependent variable and loop
derive the exact read and write index expressions for two arbitrary iterations
prove that the accessed index ranges do not overlap across iterations
rewrite loop structure to base-plus-lane, split arrays, or use temporaries so independence is syntactically visible
apply DEPENDENCE variable=<name> inter false only if the tool remains conservative
validate csim/cosim and check the achieved II report
skills.strategy: first rewrite indexing so non-overlap is explicit to the scheduler; only if the report remains conservative, apply DEPENDENCE inter false to the specific array and variable after proving safety

guards: do not use old/new buffering for algorithms that intentionally require immediate in-place Gauss-Seidel-style updates
ensure swap/copy-back occurs at the correct time-step granularity
do not double buffer arrays so large that BRAM/URAM use becomes infeasible
preserve boundary cells and unchanged elements
skills.pattern: an iterative update reads old values and writes new values through the same array, causing loop-carried RAW/WAR hazards or forcing sequential update semantics when Jacobi-style old/new separation is valid
required_steps: determine whether the algorithm can use old/new state separation without changing semantics
allocate separate input/current and output/next local buffers
load the current state into the read buffer
rewrite the compute loop to read only from old/current and write only to new/next
swap buffer roles or copy back after each iteration/time step
partition the read buffer if multiple reads per cycle block II
pipeline the compute loop and validate boundary handling
skills.strategy: split storage into old and new buffers, compute from a read-only old buffer into a write-only new buffer, and swap or copy buffers between time steps; prefer full-grid or line-buffer old/new staging over spatial tiling with per-tile global load/store inside each iteration; combine with partitioning when multiple neighbor reads are needed per cycle

guards: do not complete-partition large buffers blindly
complete partition turns storage into registers/FFs and can explode LUT/FF/routing cost
partition the dimension that is accessed in parallel, not an arbitrary dimension
this fixes local memory ports, not off-chip AXI bandwidth
skills.pattern: a small local array or a small dimension of a local buffer must provide many parallel reads/writes in a pipelined or unrolled loop, and BRAM two-port limits are the direct II bottleneck
required_steps: identify the local array reported in the port-conflict or memory-port bottleneck
confirm the array or accessed dimension is small and compile-time bounded
apply ARRAY_PARTITION complete to the accessed dimension
if only lanes are parallel, partition the lane dimension rather than the whole buffer
re-run synthesis and inspect achieved II plus FF/LUT growth
skills.strategy: fully partition the small array or small accessed dimension into registers/FFs so each element has independent access; use this aggressively only when the dimension is small enough to avoid FF/LUT explosion

guards: do not bank the wrong dimension
do not assume partitioning fixes arbitrary/conflicting indirect accesses
if several lanes can still hit the same bank, use privatization, replication, or conflict-free scheduling
avoid complete partitioning large arrays when cyclic/block banking is sufficient
skills.pattern: a BRAM-backed local buffer is accessed more than two times per cycle by a pipelined or unrolled loop, but the accesses have a regular pattern that can be distributed across banks
required_steps: count reads and writes to the buffer per target loop iteration and per unrolled lane
identify the dimension and stride of concurrent accesses
select cyclic partition for interleaved/lane-indexed accesses
select block partition when each lane or PE owns a contiguous region
rewrite loop indexing if needed so concurrent lanes map to different banks
match partition factor to unroll factor or access demand
verify each bank sees no more than feasible port demand and check achieved II
skills.strategy: rewrite indexing and choose cyclic or block banking so each BRAM bank sees no more than its supported read/write ports per cycle; match banking factor to unroll factor, stencil width, or per-iteration access count instead of immediately reducing unroll

guards: only replicate read-only or lane-private state
do not replicate large tables without resource budget
ensure all replicated copies are initialized identically
replication solves local read ports, not global memory bandwidth
skills.pattern: many unrolled lanes read the same small read-only lookup table, constants array, coefficient vector, or stencil weights, and memory-port limits prevent II=1
required_steps: identify read-only local arrays used by multiple parallel lanes
confirm the table is small enough to replicate or partition
create per-lane copies or apply complete partition to the coefficient dimension
initialize all copies consistently before the hot loop
rewrite each lane to read its own copy or partitioned element
check FF/LUT/BRAM cost against II improvement
skills.strategy: replicate the small read-only table per lane or fully partition the small coefficient dimension so each unrolled lane has an independent read path

guards: do not ignore boundary conditions or halo behavior
window update order must preserve old neighbor values before shifting
ensure line-buffer depth matches image/grid width or tile width
if the stencil has true time-step dependencies, use old/new buffers or wavefront scheduling as needed
skills.pattern: a 1D/2D stencil, convolution, image, grid, or neighbor-access loop repeatedly reads adjacent elements from global or local memory, causing port conflicts, redundant loads, or loop-carried neighbor dependencies
required_steps: identify stencil radius and neighbor access pattern
create line buffers for previous rows or shift registers for previous columns/elements
create a small fully partitioned compute window
stream new input values through the line buffer/window update each cycle
rewrite neighbor references to window entries
pipeline the main traversal loop with II=1 when legal
handle warm-up, borders, halos, and partial tiles explicitly
skills.strategy: replace repeated neighbor reads with line buffers and a sliding window/shift register; load one new element per cycle, shift local window state, compute from the partitioned window, and write valid outputs after boundary guards

guards: do not reorder true dependencies illegally
wavefront bounds are error-prone; verify start/end indices carefully
not every stencil is wavefront-parallel within a time step
preserve numerical and boundary semantics
skills.pattern: a 2D dynamic-programming, grid, or stencil-like update has true dependencies on left/top/diagonal or previous-neighbor values, and the current loop order places a dependent dimension inside the pipelined loop
required_steps: map each output dependence direction, such as left, top, top-left, previous row, or previous column
identify an iteration order where ready cells are processed after their dependencies
rewrite loops around anti-diagonals, tiles, or skewed coordinates
use rolling buffers for prior wavefronts or rows
pipeline or unroll independent cells within a wavefront when memory banking supports it
handle triangular wavefront bounds and edges
validate against the original recurrence on small cases
skills.strategy: change traversal to a wavefront/diagonal or loop-skewed order so all cells on the same wavefront are independent and can be pipelined or partially unrolled, while preserving dependency order across wavefronts

guards: do not stage unbounded arrays into local memory
DATAFLOW requires legal producer/consumer structure and bounded stream behavior
do not change host ABI or pointer types unless explicitly allowed
if each element is used once and access is already streaming, staging should still enable burst/dataflow or it may add overhead
skills.pattern: a pipelined compute loop directly issues m_axi/gmem reads and immediately consumes the response, or directly writes results, so request/response latency or AXI scheduling prevents low II
required_steps: identify m_axi reads/writes inside the II-limited compute loop
split global load, compute, and global store into separate loops or functions
make load/store addresses contiguous and burst-friendly where possible
stage bounded chunks into local buffers or streams
apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope when stages can run concurrently
use ping-pong buffers for tiled/chunked stages when the same buffer would serialize load and compute
set appropriate burst length and outstanding transaction pragmas where legal
pipeline compute over local memory and validate burst/report behavior
skills.strategy: decouple global-memory request/response from compute by splitting load, compute, and store stages; use burst-friendly load/store loops, local buffers or hls::stream FIFOs, DATAFLOW, and optionally ping-pong buffering to keep compute working on local data

guards: do not prefetch indirect or data-dependent addresses unless correctness and bounds are guaranteed
prefetch depth must fit local memory and avoid FIFO deadlock
outstanding transaction pragmas may not help if access pattern is non-burstable
preserve ordering when memory side effects or aliasing matter
skills.pattern: the compute pipeline stalls waiting for global-memory responses even though future addresses are known early enough to prefetch or issue longer bursts
required_steps: confirm future read addresses are predictable before data is consumed
rewrite accesses to monotonic contiguous bursts when legal
create a local prefetch buffer, FIFO, or tile cache with bounded depth
pipeline the prefetch loop and the compute loop separately
set num_read_outstanding and max_read_burst_length on relevant m_axi ports
guard prefetch distance, tails, and bounds
inspect reports for actual burst inference and outstanding behavior
skills.strategy: issue burst-friendly prefetches into a local queue, stream, or tile buffer ahead of compute; increase safe outstanding transactions and burst length so memory latency is hidden behind local computation

guards: do not interchange loops when it violates data dependencies or output order
manual loop interchange is not useful if the tool already performs it and no access pattern changes
after reordering, partition the dimension actually accessed in parallel
verify boundaries and row-major/column-major indexing carefully
skills.pattern: a loop nest misses II because the innermost pipelined loop uses strided/non-contiguous global accesses, repeatedly hits the same local memory bank, or places the dependency-carrying dimension in the hot pipeline
required_steps: identify current inner-loop memory stride and dependency direction
determine whether loop interchange or strip-mining preserves semantics
choose an inner dimension with contiguous global access or conflict-free bank mapping
update local buffer layout and ARRAY_PARTITION dim to match the new inner loop
rewrite index expressions and boundary/tail handling
pipeline the new hot loop and inspect burst/II reports
skills.strategy: reorder or strip-mine loops so the pipelined inner loop is unit-stride for global memory, maps parallel lanes to distinct local banks, or moves true dependencies to an outer sequential dimension when legal

guards: do not change numerical precision or arithmetic semantics without tolerance support
do not duplicate expensive operators until memory can feed the added compute
operator binding is tool/platform sensitive and must be validated by synthesis reports
if the real bottleneck is memory, use memory skills first
skills.pattern: the achieved II is limited by arithmetic operator availability, high-latency operations, or resource sharing rather than memory ports or false dependencies
required_steps: identify the operator reported as the II/resource bottleneck
check for loop-invariant or repeated arithmetic that can be hoisted or precomputed
replace division/modulo/sqrt or expensive floating-point operations only when numerical requirements allow
use balanced reduction trees for associative expressions
consider fixed-point or narrower integer types when precision permits
bind operators to suitable resources if the default mapping is poor
compare resource growth, timing, and achieved II
skills.strategy: restructure expensive arithmetic instead of only reducing unroll: replace divides with reciprocal/multiply when legal, precompute loop-invariant expressions, use balanced trees for reductions, choose fixed-point or narrower types when acceptable, and ensure operators are bound/pipelined appropriately

guards: do not privatize state that intentionally coordinates lanes or enforces order
ensure state initialization and finalization are correct for each lane
watch local memory growth from replication
if lane-local state changes output order, preserve original mapping explicitly
skills.pattern: multiple unrolled lanes or processing elements contend for one shared variable, state object, random-number state, lookup state, or accumulator resource, creating a serialized resource or dependence bottleneck
required_steps: identify shared state accessed by multiple lanes or PEs in the hot loop
determine whether the state can be made independent per lane or per work item
reshape state as state[LANES][...] or state[PE][...]
partition the lane/PE dimension completely
rewrite each lane to access only its own state
merge or copy back final state only if semantically required
skills.strategy: make state lane-local or PE-local, partition the state dimension completely, and merge or reconcile state after the parallel section when needed

guards: do not create cyclic streams without a proven schedule
producer and consumer token counts must match or be explicitly framed
DATAFLOW does not remove true data dependencies
stream depth tuning is required for variable-latency stages
skills.pattern: one stage in a loop body has variable or long latency, such as memory access, filtering, parsing, or conditional work, and it serializes otherwise independent producer/consumer work
required_steps: identify separable producer/compute/consumer work in the loop body
extract stages into functions or loops with clear interfaces
connect stages with hls::stream or bounded local FIFOs
set stream depth large enough to absorb burstiness but small enough for resources
apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope
guard stream counts so producer and consumer agree exactly
validate no deadlock and inspect dataflow viewer/report
skills.strategy: split the loop body into producer, compute, and consumer stages connected by hls::stream FIFOs under DATAFLOW, so backpressure is localized and independent stages can run concurrently

guards: complete partition is effective for small arrays and small lane dimensions, not arbitrary large storage
large complete partition can destroy timing even if II improves in scheduling
do not use resource-heavy partitioning to mask an off-chip bandwidth bottleneck
skills.pattern: a proposed fix completely partitions a large local buffer or large multidimensional tile into registers only because there is a memory dependency or port conflict
required_steps: detect whether complete partition is being applied to a large array or large tile
estimate FF/LUT/routing growth from full partitioning
identify the actual parallel access dimension and access count
prefer cyclic/block partitioning, reshape, local banking, or small lane-buffer complete partition
validate whether the alternative resolves II without resource explosion
skills.strategy: do not use complete partition as the default for large buffers; instead choose cyclic/block banking, line buffers, smaller tiles, per-lane small buffers, or algorithmic privatization targeted to the actual access pattern

guards: false-dependence pragmas can silently produce incorrect hardware when applied to true hazards
do not prioritize II=1 over semantic correctness
if exact sequential order is required, algorithmic restructuring may not be legal
skills.pattern: a proposed fix uses DEPENDENCE inter false on an array or accumulator that is truly read and written across iterations, such as a reduction, histogram, in-place update, or same-address read-modify-write
required_steps: check whether two iterations can access the same location with at least one write
classify the dependence as reduction, scatter/RMW, stencil/in-place update, or inherent recurrence
route to partial accumulators, privatization, old/new buffering, wavefront, or best-legal-II handling
remove unsafe false-dependence pragma proposals
validate correctness before measuring II
skills.strategy: reject the false-dependence pragma and use a legal transformation instead: partial sums for reductions, privatized accumulators for RMW/scatter, old/new buffers for Jacobi-style updates, or accept the legal II for inherently serial recurrences

skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
guards: preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port

skills.pattern: kernel touches m_axi pointer ports in compute loops and may benefit from pipelining, unroll, or DATAFLOW but must not bottleneck on repeated external memory RMW
skills.strategy: Use explicit load-compute-store: (1) load required inputs from m_axi into local on-chip buffers or private scalars; (2) perform all repeated updates, reductions, and accumulations on locals only; (3) store final results back to m_axi outputs once per element when possible. Prefer burst-friendly sequential loads/stores and separate phases.
required_steps: identify every m_axi port used in compute
add local buffers for reused arrays and private scalar accumulators for reductions
pipeline load, compute, and store loops independently where legal
write each output m_axi element at most once per logical update (after local finalize)
apply tiling when full arrays exceed on-chip budget while keeping RMW off m_axi inside inner loops
guards: do not change top-level pointer element types unless explicitly allowed
pair with distinct gmemN bundles per port when parallelizing external access
local arrays must be sized with fixed bounds from header macros
